blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Persistent pollution and gaps in marine rehabilitation threaten fisheries and food security in the Verde Island Passage (VIP), an environmental group warned Friday, citing elevated oil-and-grease levels and declining seagrass cover in marine protected areas in Oriental Mindoro. The Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development (CEED) issued the warning on World Food Day, as the country prepares to participate in the 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17).
